articleBlocks: Puzzle #752 opens with Motor, Damage, Quality, Remote, and Air traffic, a set of clues that appear to belong to completely different categories on first read. That spread is what makes the board deceptive: instead of pointing toward a single subject area, the clues push you toward toys, brands, folklore, or everyday vocabulary all at once. When Pinpoint does this, the safer move is to stop grouping by topic and start testing whether the same missing word can complete every clue naturally.

That approach resolves this board quickly. The shared connector is "control". Once you test "control" across the full list, each phrase settles into a clean compound and the noise disappears. The answer is the phrase pattern where every clue comes before control, and it works because it explains the whole set with the same exact move. If one connector completes all five without stretching the meaning, that is usually the correct Pinpoint solution.
solutionNarrative: I tested each clue against the same connector and checked whether the phrase stayed natural. For #752, Motor, Damage, Quality, Remote, and Air traffic consistently map to words that come before control. Motor control can describe movement regulation, damage control describes limiting harm, quality control checks standards, remote control operates a device, and air traffic control coordinates flights. That shared fit across all five clues is why the control-phrase pattern is the correct answer. The important step is not spotting one familiar phrase; it is confirming that every clue takes the same word after it without changing the rule.
